Overloaded Constructors Chain with this(...) to One That Checks and Assigns

recorded.prompt:q-mapper-after-new-constructor: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapper-after-new-constructor: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapper-after-new-constructor: Correct option a. Page: "Declaring a constructor removes the default one. javac doesn't check reflective calls, so the failure waited for the first request." and the shown output "java.lang.NoSuchMethodException: Subscription.<init>()". Both halves (build passes, first mapping throws) are stated.
recorded.prompt:q-range-parse-before-this: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-range-parse-before-this: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-range-parse-before-this: Correct option b. Page: "A this(...) or super(...) call must be the first statement. Parsing a spec such as \"cpu>90\" before delegating fails with `call to this must be first statement in constructor`. ... Compute arguments with static methods inside the call", followed by the example this(metricOf(spec), limitOf(spec)). The reference table is headed "Constructor rules (Java 21)" and lists "statement before this(...) or super(...) | compile error", which matches the stem's Java 21.
recorded.prompt:q-session-registered-then-throws: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-registered-then-throws: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-registered-then-throws: Correct option c. Page: "The second constructor threw and `new` returned nothing, but the feed already held the object." and "The feed holds a reference, not a copy: on the same thread, every field the constructor assigned before throwing shows through it." The user field was assigned before the throw, so it shows through the registry's reference.
recorded.prompt:q-identity-of-factory-result: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-identity-of-factory-result: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-identity-of-factory-result: Correct option c. Page: "Rely on identity or class only where the javadoc promises it", "`Currency` promises one instance per currency; `List.of` promises only an unmodifiable `List`", and "`==` ... is true only when a factory returns the same object." Being documented to return "the region with that code" is not a promise of one instance.

recorded.prompt:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:b: Page: "Declaring a constructor removes the default one." Java does not keep the supplied constructor. Partly true: "the build passes" is correct; only the outcome and the reason are wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:c: Page: "javac doesn't check reflective calls, so the failure waited for the first request." So the build does not fail.
recorded.prompt:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mapper-after-new-constructor:d: Page: "Declaring a constructor removes the default one." The default has "no parameters" and "Constructors are told apart only by their parameter types", so a (String) constructor cannot clash with it. The page never says outright that adding a constructor causes no clash, but this follows from the removal rule.
recorded.prompt:q-range-parse-before-this:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-range-parse-before-this:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-range-parse-before-this:a: Page: "The copied constructor skipped the check and the normalisation." and the summary: "A copied overload skips the checks". So the other constructor's check does not run. Partly true: "It doesn't compile" is correct; only the suggested fix is wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-range-parse-before-this:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-range-parse-before-this:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-range-parse-before-this:c: Page: "A this(...) or super(...) call must be the first statement" and the table: "statement before this(...) or super(...) | compile error" (Java 21). So it can't come anywhere. Partly true only on a later release: "Unit 2.1.1 shows what Java 25 relaxes." The stem pins Java 21, so the option is still wrong.
recorded.prompt:q-range-parse-before-this:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-range-parse-before-this:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-range-parse-before-this:d: Refuted on compilation: the statement before this(...) "fails with `call to this must be first statement in constructor`". The page doesn't say "this(...) is never an ordinary call" (the option's `says`), but refuting "it compiles" is enough.
recorded.prompt:q-session-registered-then-throws:: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-registered-then-throws:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-registered-then-throws: Page: "the feed already held the object. It answers every price for as long as the feed lives." and the table: "references handed out before the throw still reach the half-built object". Nothing is undone. Partly true: "the token check threw before the constructor finished" is accurate.
recorded.prompt:q-session-registered-then-throws:: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-registered-then-throws:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-registered-then-throws: Page: "The feed called `onPrice` before the fields were assigned". The feed had and used the object while the constructor was still running, and "the feed already held the object". Partly true: "add(this) ran while the constructor was still running" is accurate.
recorded.prompt:q-session-registered-then-throws:: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-session-registered-then-throws:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-session-registered-then-throws: Page: "The feed holds a reference, not a copy: on the same thread, every field the constructor assigned before throwing shows through it." Partly true: "add(this) ran before the user was assigned" is accurate, and the page's own output ("ALERT null") shows null during the constructor, which makes this distractor tempting. The reference-not-copy sentence resolves it.
recorded.prompt:q-identity-of-factory-result:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-identity-of-factory-result:a: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-identity-of-factory-result:a: Same rule: "Rely on identity or class only where the javadoc promises it". The page contrasts Currency's explicit one-instance promise with List.of's weaker promise. A promise about content is not a promise about identity.
recorded.prompt:q-identity-of-factory-result:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-identity-of-factory-result:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-identity-of-factory-result:b: Page: "A factory may return an existing one" (may, not must), and the table says the result "may be cached". Temperature has a private constructor, yet ofCelsius does `return new Temperature(...)` on every call, which is a counterexample, and "The private constructor forces every caller through `watch`" presents a private constructor as routing only. The page never says outright that a private constructor doesn't imply reuse; it has to be inferred.
recorded.prompt:q-identity-of-factory-result:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-identity-of-factory-result:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-identity-of-factory-result:d: Page: "`==` compares references (unit 1.1.2), so it is true only when a factory returns the same object." It never compares codes. Partly true: the verdict "No" is correct; only the reason is wrong.
